details: CONFIRMED by reading. The brief points at "D's rule text ... (sections 3, 6, 7)"; design section 3, D item 3 "What a
wave is under D" says the line at front SKILL.md 153 "becomes" a new definition, with rule text "in the front skill
and rules/git.md". The change adds the hold and the green-run train but leaves line 153 as it was, and the Lanes
section's "When a lane finishes, start the next call at once" removes the pause the old wave rule relied on. The
design's worked case (two syncs a day) only holds if the next paid run starts on the waiting train's head; the new
text says "After each green run, relay sync, then the waiting changes land as one train" and stops there.
Size: 15 agent minutes (rule text and one needle in test_lanes).
evidence: grep -n 'Texts get one paid run per wave' plugins/front/skills/front/SKILL.md
153:... Texts get one paid run per wave: after the last merge of a wave of 3-4
design-speed.md D.3: "The front skill's 'after the last merge of a wave of 3-4 changes (not while it is half-merged)'
becomes: a wave is the train of checked-path changes landed after a green run ...; the paid run starts right after
that train has fully landed, when `due` lists at least `wave_min` changes, or at the end of a work stretch"
git diff master...HEAD -- plugins/front/skills/front/SKILL.md: only lines 168-184 added; line 153 unchanged.
failing_case: 6 lanes run; changes land one by one every 15-30 minutes, never pausing; no paid run is going and `bin/paid-cost due`
lists 2 changes. The front skill (line 153) still says the paid run starts "after the last merge of a wave of 3-4
changes (not while it is half-merged)". Under lanes there is no last merge: the next change is always half a cycle
away. Now: the front has no rule for when to start the run (it may never start one, or start one after every merge).
Should: the text says what the design D.3 says: a wave is the train of checked-path changes landed after a green run
(plus what landed beside it); the paid run starts right after that train has fully landed, or when `due` lists at
least 3 changes, or at the end of a work stretch whatever `due` holds; after a green run's waiting train lands, the
next paid run starts on that head.
fix_hint: Rewrite the sentence at line 153 to D.3's definition (wave = the train landed after a green run; start the paid run
on that head once it has fully landed, or when `due` lists 3+ changes, or at the end of a work stretch), and add
"then start the next paid run on that head" to the Lanes paragraph; mirror one line in rules/git.md.
pass_cases: 1. Artifact: the front skill defines a wave under lanes in one place (line 153 or the Lanes section), matching design D.3: the train of checked-path changes landed after a green run starts the next paid run on that head.
2. Artifact: the front skill names a trigger that does not need lanes to pause: `due` lists at least 3 changes (the old "3-4"), or the end of a work stretch.
3. Artifact: rules/git.md "after a wave of merges" stays consistent with the front's definition (same words or a pointer).
4. Kept: "no paid run is going" and the daily cap check still gate the start (bin/paid-cost today / bin/ci refusal).
reason: tests/test_lanes.py:100-ish Wave::test_front_defines_wave_and_the_three_endings and test_wave_min_default_and_bounds pass; front SKILL.md defines the wave, triggers (train landed, due >= wave_min, end of stretch); git.md consistent; fail on base.
findings.summary: D's new wave definition is missing: with lanes landing continuously, 'after the last merge of a wave of 3-4 changes' never happens, so when the paid run starts is undefined

details: CONFIRMED by reading the front skill as a whole: line 161-165 (a red run adds one fix item and "the next wave's run
proves the fix"; a not-judged run is "run it again after the next wave") and line 182-183 (waiting changes "stay
waiting behind it"). Under the hold, the checked-path changes that would form "the next wave" are exactly the held
ones, so the two rules wait on each other. The design D.2 says "When it is red, the fix for the red goes first
(principle 1) and the waiting changes land after the next green run", which still needs the next run to start without
a wave; the text does not say so. Six lanes make it likely: 56% of changes touch checked paths (design, measured).
Size: 15 agent minutes.
evidence: plugins/front/skills/front/SKILL.md:161-165 "the next wave's run proves the fix ... A run that is not a pass without a
failing eval (money ceiling, runs not judged, the day's cap) adds no item: tell the owner in one line and run it again
after the next wave."
plugins/front/skills/front/SKILL.md:181-183 "After each green run, `relay sync`, then the waiting changes land as one
train (above). A red run is the fix item described above; the waiting changes stay waiting behind it."
failing_case: A paid run goes; 4 changes touching rules/ and plugins/*/skills/ wait at the landing. Case a: the run ends red. The
text says "the waiting changes stay waiting behind it" (behind the fix item? until the next green run?). The fix item
lands alone; the next paid run starts "after the last merge of a wave of 3-4 changes", but the 4 checked-path changes
are held until a green run: the run waits for a wave and the wave waits for a green run. Case b: the run stops on the
money ceiling or the day's cap (not green, not red: "run it again after the next wave"); the text says the waiting
changes wait "until the run ends" and land "after each green run": it ended, it is not green, nothing says whether they
land. Should: one stated release for each ending: green (sync, then the waiting train, then the next run on its head);
red (the fix lands first; then the next paid run starts on the fix's head at once, and the waiting changes land after
it goes green, as design D.2 says); not judged (the waiting changes land as one train and the run is retried on that
head, or they keep waiting for the retried run: one of the two, stated).
fix_hint: Replace the last sentence of the Lanes section with the three endings: green (as now, then the next run on the
train's head); red (the fix lands first, the next paid run starts on its head without waiting for a wave, the waiting
changes land after it is green); not judged (state one choice). F1's wave text can carry the "no wave needed" part.
pass_cases: 1. Artifact: the Lanes section says what releases the waiting changes after a red run, in a way that does not need those changes to form a wave (e.g. "the fix item lands, the next paid run starts on its head at once, the waiting changes land after it is green").
2. Artifact: the Lanes section says what happens to the waiting changes after a run that is neither green nor red (ceiling, cap, runs not judged).
3. Kept artifact: after a green run, `relay sync` runs before the waiting train lands (line "After each green run, `relay sync`, then the waiting changes land as one train").
4. Kept artifact: a change that touches no checked path lands as usual during a paid run.
reason: tests/test_lanes.py Wave::test_front_defines_wave_and_the_three_endings (- Green:, - Red:, - Not judged); SKILL.md lists the three endings; fails on base.
findings.summary: after a red or not-judged paid run the waiting changes have no release: 'stay waiting behind it' plus the wave rule can wait on each other

details: CONFIRMED by reading: front SKILL.md 153-157 runs bin/ci "in a detached worktree of the default branch's head"; design
D.1 "The paid run already runs detached in its own worktree (.worktrees/paid-<sha>)"; design D.2 gives the reason as
sync staying refused. A rule text that relay ships to every project's front states a mechanism that is not true.
Size: 5 agent minutes.
evidence: plugins/front/skills/front/SKILL.md:180 "landing it would change what the run is judging"
plugins/front/skills/front/SKILL.md:155-156 "... in a detached worktree of the default branch's head, so the primary checkout stays clean"
design-speed.md D.2: "If they kept landing during every paid run, `due` would never be empty and sync would stay refused all day."
failing_case: The front reads line 180: a checked-path change waits "because landing it would change what the run is judging". Line
155 of the same file says the paid run runs "in a detached worktree of the default branch's head", so a landing on
the default branch changes nothing the run reads. A model that notices the contradiction can drop the hold as
pointless (then `due` lists the landed change after the green run and `relay sync` stays refused all day, the waste
design D.2 measured: 30 of 54 branches touch checked paths); one that believes it may hold other things for the same
wrong reason. Should: the reason given is the true one: a checked-path change landed during the run is not covered by
it, so `bin/paid-cost due` would not be empty after a green run and `relay sync` would stay refused.
fix_hint: "... waits at the landing until the run ends: the run does not cover it, so after a green run `bin/paid-cost due`
would still list it and `relay sync` would stay refused."
pass_cases: 1. Artifact: the Lanes paragraph gives the reason as `relay sync` refusing while `bin/paid-cost due` lists a change, and no longer says landing changes what the run judges.
2. Kept artifact: line 155's "in a detached worktree of the default branch's head" stays.
3. Kept artifact: rules/git.md and the delegate skill keep the hold without a contradicting reason.
reason: Same test asserts the false sentence is absent and "relay sync would stay refused" present; detached-worktree line kept.
findings.summary: the hold's stated reason is false: the paid run judges a detached worktree, landing does not change what it judges; the real reason (keep `due` empty so sync can run) is not given

details: CONFIRMED by reading: the rule texts say "a change whose files match `bin/paid-cost paths`"; no code computes the
match and plugins/core/hooks/merge.py does not refuse a landing during a paid run (design D's test "the land step
refuses a branch whose diff touches a checked path" belongs to the landing item, ip 96, not built here). Project rule:
principle 5 (fact to code, meaning to the model). LOW: the matching globs are few and the miss costs a delay, not data.
Size: 15 agent minutes.
evidence: git grep -n 'paid-cost paths' -> rules/git.md:19, front SKILL.md:178, delegate SKILL.md:86 (prose only)
bin/paid-cost:211-213: paths prints the globs; no subcommand takes a branch.
failing_case: A paid run goes; wt/x changes `plugins/front/skills/front/SKILL.md` and `lib/relay_gate.py`. The front must compare
its file list with the globs `plugins/*/skills/**`, `rules/**`, ... printed by `bin/paid-cost paths`, by reading (or
by composing `git diff --name-only master...wt/x -- <globs>` itself). Now: the decision is a model's glob match; a
miss lands the change (sync blocked until the next paid run), a false match holds a change for up to 110 minutes.
Should: one command prints the answer, e.g. `bin/paid-cost touches wt/x` (or `paths --branch wt/x`) prints the
matching files and exits 1 when there are none.
fix_hint: Add `touches <ref>` to bin/paid-cost: `git diff --name-only <default>...<ref> -- *CHECKED_PATHS`, print, exit 0/1;
the three rule texts name it instead of "files match".
pass_cases: 1. `bin/paid-cost touches <branch>` on a branch changing plugins/front/skills/front/SKILL.md prints that path, exit 0.
2. The same on a branch changing only lib/relay_gate.py prints nothing, exit 1.
3. A branch changing plugins/core/hooks/merge.py matches (plugins/*/hooks/**); one changing plugins/delegate/workflows/cycle.js does not (not in CHECKED_PATHS today).
4. Kept: `bin/paid-cost paths` prints the 7 globs without ":(glob)".
reason: tests/test_lanes.py Touches::test_checked_path_is_printed_exit_0 and test_unchecked_paths_print_nothing_exit_1 pass, fail on base; hook path matches, cycle.js does not.
findings.summary: whether a branch touches the checked paths is left to the model's eye (principle 5: fact to code); no command answers it and the merge hook does not hold the landing

details: CONFIRMED by reading: rules/delegation.md 44 drops "unless the project says otherwise" and adds "in one change";
lib/relay_rules.py LANES_DEFAULT = 4 is written into every project file. The brief set "default 4", so this is the
front's reading of the old agent cap as a change cap, not an owner decision; the design proposed default 3, bound 1-4.
Not measured: load and rate limits at 16 agents. Question for the owner, not a defect. Size: 5 agent minutes either way.

"- At most 4 agents at once in one change; ... (projects.toml `lanes`, 1-8, default 4)."
lib/relay_gate.py:31 DEFAULT_SLOTS = 3

CLAUDE.local.md says "Changes built at once: 4." and the delegation rule caps 4 agents per change: up to 16 agents and
4 cycle runs at once, with 3 gate slots on the machine. The owner's answer of 27 Oct ("Давай 6 сразу") was about
relay. Should: the owner decides the default for projects that set nothing (4 lanes as built, or 1 = today's
behaviour), and whether the agent cap is per change or overall.
fix_hint: Ask the owner; if the answer is 1 for other projects, set LANES_DEFAULT = 1 and the "default" in the texts.

words: 6. Это конфигуриремый параметр для каждого проекта, в relay это будет 6

2. Artifact: LANES_DEFAULT in lib/relay_rules.py and the "default N" in rules/delegation.md and the front skill match that answer.
reason: Owner question; owner answered 2026-10-27 that lanes is a per-project setting and relay uses 6. Left untouched by the fixer; the default for other projects is still 4, recorded as the owner's word.
